Head_and_Face: Head is small relative to body length.
Mouth is blunt and slightly downturned.
Two short barbels present at each corner of the mouth.
Eyes are small and positioned laterally.
Iris is reddish-orange.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is elongated and laterally compressed.
Scales are small, deeply embedded, and cycloid, giving a smooth, slimy texture.
Dorsal surface coloration ranges from olive-green to golden-bronze.
Ventral surface fades to pale yellow-white.
Lateral line is complete and distinctly visible as a pale curved line running mid-laterally from operculum to caudal peduncle.
Skin texture is characteristically mucous-coated.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Dorsal fin is short and rounded.
Caudal fin is truncate to slightly emarginate.
Fins exhibit a dark gray to olive hue without prominent markings.

Head_and_Face: Head is short.
Mouth is terminal and lacks barbels.
Eyes are large and prominent, positioned high on the head.
Opercular region may display an iridescent golden patch.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is laterally compressed, ovoid to fusiform.
Scales are large, easily visible, and cycloid.
Coloration ranges from metallic orange-red to golden-yellow in domestic specimens.
Some individuals exhibit calico patterns of orange, white, and black patches.
Wild-type specimens are dull olive-green dorsally with silvery-white ventral surfaces.
Scales exhibit a reflective, metallic sheen under illumination.
Fin membranes are translucent with coloration matching the body.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Dorsal fin is long-based with 15-20 rays, extending from mid-back.
Caudal fin is deeply forked in wild types.
Ornamental varieties may have double-tailed or fantail caudal fins.

class_name: great white shark, white shark, man-eater, man-eating shark, Carcharodon carcharias

Head_and_Face: Snout is conical and pointed.
Eyes are large, round, and black.
Mouth is wide and arched.
Teeth are large, triangular, and serrated, arranged in a continuous cutting edge.
Five prominent gill slits visible anterior to the pectoral fins.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust and torpedo-shaped (fusiform).
Surface covered in dermal denticles creating a rough, sandpaper-like texture.
Exhibits countershading: dark gray to slate-gray dorsally.
Sharp demarcation from clean white ventral surface along the lateral midline.
No prominent body markings or spots.
Uniform gray-white contrast is a key diagnostic feature.
Lateral line system visible as a series of pore openings along the flanks.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Pectoral fins are large, falcate (sickle-shaped), and positioned low on the body.
First dorsal fin is tall and triangular, originating posterior to the pectoral fin free tip.
Second dorsal fin is markedly smaller.
Caudal fin is lunate (crescent-shaped) with nearly symmetrical upper and lower lobes.

Head_and_Face: Snout is broad and blunt.
Mouth is wide.
Teeth are heavily serrated, curved, with a distinctive hooked tip.
Five gill slits are present.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is stocky and cylindrical.
Surface covered in rough dermal denticles.
Dorsal coloration is grayish-blue to greenish-gray.
Ventral surface is pale gray to white.
Dark gray to black transverse bars, spots, and stripes along the flanks and dorsal surface, resembling tiger striping.
A prominent interdorsal ridge runs along the midline between the two dorsal fins.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Pectoral fins are broad and rounded.
First dorsal fin is relatively small and positioned far posterior, originating over or behind the pectoral fin insertion.
Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a well-developed lower lobe and a pronounced subterminal notch on the upper lobe.

Head_and_Face: Head is laterally expanded and dorsoventrally flattened, resembling a hammer or T-shape (cephalofoil).
Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
Nostrils are located at the anterior margin of the cephalofoil, separated by a broad medial indentation.
Five gill slits visible on the ventrolateral surface.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is streamlined and fusiform.
Surface covered in fine dermal denticles giving a rough texture.
Coloration is olive-gray to brown dorsally, fading to white ventrally.
No prominent markings or stripes.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate, originating over or slightly anterior to the pectoral fin insertion.
Pectoral fins are moderately falcate.
Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a prominent upper lobe and subterminal notch.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are small and positioned dorsally on the head.
Spiracles are large and prominent, located immediately posterior to the eyes.
Mouth and nostrils are ventrally positioned.
Body_and_Plumage: Body disc is nearly circular to oval, formed by fusion of enlarged pectoral fins to the head and trunk.
Disc surface is smooth, soft, and gelatinous, lacking rough dermal denticles.
Dorsal coloration is uniform dark brown, gray, or reddish-brown.
Often exhibits mottled or marbled patterns.
Ventral surface is pale white to cream.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Tail is thick, muscular, and shorter than the body disc.
Two dorsal fins are present on the tail.
Caudal fin is well-developed.

Head_and_Face: Eyes and spiracles are positioned dorsally on the head.
Mouth, nostrils, and five gill slits are ventrally positioned.
Body_and_Plumage: Body disc is dorsoventrally flattened, formed by broad, wing-like pectoral fins fused to the head.
Disc shape varies from diamond to circular.
Dorsal surface is smooth to granular, covered in small dermal denticles or tubercles.
Coloration is typically olive-brown, gray, or sandy dorsally.
Ventral surface is white to pale cream.
Disc surface may exhibit small thorn-like denticles along the midline in some species.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Tail is elongated, whip-like, and significantly longer than the body disc.
One or more serrated, venomous caudal spines (barbs) located on the dorsal surface of the tail near its base.
Tail lacks dorsal fins.

Head_and_Face: Comb is large, fleshy, serrated (single or rose type), bright red to crimson, standing erect.
A pair of pendulous red wattles hangs from the lower mandible.
Beak is short, curved, and horn-colored (yellow to gray).
Eyes are round with a reddish-brown iris and a distinct pale orbital ring.
Body_and_Plumage: Plumage exhibits iridescent green-black feathers on the neck (hackles) and saddle.
Body feathers in red, brown, black, or white depending on breed.
Posture is upright with broad shoulders.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Tail features long, arching, iridescent sickle feathers that curve upward and backward.
Legs are unfeathered, scaly, with a rough keratinous texture, colored yellow to gray.
Three forward-facing toes and one rear-facing hallux, each with a sharp curved claw.
A prominent spur projects from the posterior tarsometatarsus.

Head_and_Face: Comb is small, fleshy, pale red to pinkish, often floppy or partially developed.
Wattles are reduced or absent.
Beak is short, slightly curved, and horn-colored (yellow to gray).
Eyes are round with a reddish-brown iris and a pale orbital ring.
Body_and_Plumage: Plumage is uniform and subdued, lacking iridescent hackle and saddle feathers.
Body feathers are typically brown, red, black, white, or barred depending on breed.
Body contour is rounded and compact.
Abdomen (vent region) is broader and deeper.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Tail is short with straight, non-arched feathers, lacking sickle feathers.
Legs are unfeathered, scaly with a rough keratinous texture, colored yellow to gray.
Three forward-facing toes and one rear-facing hallux with curved claws.
Spurs are absent or present only as small, undeveloped bumps.

Head_and_Face: Head is small relative to body size.
Eyes are large, framed by long, prominent eyelashes.
Beak is broad, flat, and horn-colored.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is massive, the largest of any living bird.
Plumage is soft, fluffy, and filamentous, lacking interlocking barbules, giving a shaggy, disheveled appearance.
Males exhibit black body plumage with white primary and secondary wing feathers and white tail plumes.
Females are uniformly grayish-brown.
Neck is elongated and nearly featherless, with pink to gray skin.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are extremely long and powerful, covered in scaly skin.
Each leg has only two toes: a large inner toe bearing a hoof-like claw and a smaller outer toe.
Legs are pinkish in males, grayish in females.
Wings are reduced, with two functional digits bearing claws.
Tail is a short tuft of decorative plumes.
